brief.recommendation: Checkout success 77% vs SLO 95%; revenue at risk $4,155/min. Waiting ~896s costs ~$62,039 and EXCEEDS the 60s tolerated degradation. Terminating batch_replayable_inventory (class BATCH_REPLAYABLE, replayable, may_interrupt, replay cost 4 min) costs a 4-minute replay of inventory_reconcile. audit.report: The checkout API experienced a 45% success rate drop (77% vs 95% SLO) due to a blocked batch_replayable_inventory job held open 4.1s by an idle transaction. The database guardian recommended waiting, but the continuity guardian overrode this, citing that the expected 896s runtime would cost ~$62k in lost checkout revenue, exceeding the 60s business degradation tolerance. The pact ultimately agreed to terminate the batch job after 2 rounds. The termination was blocked by an authority veto (failed role_allowlist, app_allowlist, live_identity, and no_protected_settlement checks) before the target pid 146763 could be killed, leaving the system in a DENIED state.
audit.root_cause: An idle transaction held open 4.1s by the batch_replayable_inventory job blocked checkout sessions, and the guardians could not agree on whether to wait for natural completion or terminate the replayable workload.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian wasted one round proposing wait despite the 896s expected runtime clearly exceeding the 60s tolerated degradation, while the continuity guardian correctly identified the cost exposure but the pact's 2-round agreement was short‑circuited by authority vetoes on the terminate action.
follow_ups: Audit the role_allowlist and app_allowlist entries for the batch_replayable_inventory and checkout_api workloads to ensure terminate commands are permitted in future pacts.
Add a pre‑negotiation checklist that compares expected remaining runtime against the business degradation tolerance window before the first wait-round is proposed.
Log the target pid and usename in the authority denial payload so teams can distinguish between role/app mismatches and protected‑settlement conflicts.

events.title: R2 proposes terminate:batch_replayable_inventory

proposal.rationale: The Continuity Guardian correctly identifies that waiting exceeds the 60s business degradation tolerance with an expected remaining runtime of ~896s, costing ~$62,039 in checkout revenue at the current loss rate. The blocking transaction is idle in transaction at 4.1s, but will not finish within the 60s tolerated window. The workload is replayable (BIZ-2) with policy may_interrupt (BIZ-2), and no protected settlements are in flight (DB-2). Terminating ends the lock wait immediately, releasing the 12 blocked checkout sessions, at the cost of a 4-minute replay of inventory_reconcile. This is the only candidate that prevents sustained SLO violation and revenue loss beyond the 60s tolerance. Waiting would continue to cost ~$62k and exceed degradation tolerance. Escalating defers a time-critical decision to a human owner when the trade-off is already quantified. TERMINATE is the correct action given the invariants: workload registry present (BIZ-2), change calendar present (BIZ-3), no protected settlements (DB-2), and tradeoff computed (BIZ-4).
proposal.expected_effect: Terminating pid 152225 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory) will release its locks, immediately unblocking the 12 checkout sessions waiting on locks. Checkout should recover within seconds, restoring success rate toward the 95% SLO. The trade-off is a single 4-minute replay of inventory_reconcile (idempotent, resumes from last checkpoint) to re-process any inventory state changes that were in-flight during the terminated transaction. No protected settlements are affected (DB-2).
proposal.risk_assessment: The only risk is the 4-minute replay of inventory_reconcile to rebuild inventory state from the terminated transaction's last checkpoint. This is an idempotent, replayable batch job (BIZ-2, policy may_interrupt). No data loss or corruption is expected; the job will resume correctly. No protected settlements are in flight (DB-2), so no financial settlement risk. The replay cost is explicitly authorized by the may_interrupt policy.
changes: Proposed terminate instead of wait in response to Continuity Guardian's objection that waiting exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance with ~$62k revenue at risk and 896s expected remaining runtime.
